PRAYING TO ALLOW THIS CRIMINAL PETITION AND QUASH THE FIR AND COMPLAINT IN CRIME NO.154/2022 FOR OFFENCES UNDER SECTIONS 419, 420, 409, 465, 467, 468, 471 R/W 149 OF IPC ON THE FILE OF SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC, MUDDEBIHAL AS AGAINST THE PETITIONER WHO IS ACCUSED NO.2 IN THE ABOVE CASE, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.

THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Accused No.2 is before this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings as against him in Crime No.154/2022 registered by Muddebihal Police Station,
Vijayapur for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 409, 465, 467, 468, 471 read with Section 149 of IPC, which is now pending on the file of the learned Senior Civil Judge and JMFC,
Muddebihal.
2.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is a practicing advocate and he is a notary appointed by the Union of India.
He submits that there is no complaint from any aggrieved persons that the petitioner had notarized the general power of attorney in NC: 2024:KHC-K:4779 the absence of such party.
He also submits that in view of Section 13 of the Notaries Act, 1952, in the absence of any sanction from the competent authority, the petitioner cannot be prosecuted.

Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
3.
Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 has opposed the petition.

4. The FIR in Crime No.154/2022 was registered against five accused persons for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information submitted by Shivanand Sagar- Special Land Acquisition Officer, Upper Krishna Project, Almatti.

The allegation in the first information against the petitioner is that he had notarized the power of attorney, on the basis of which, accused No.1 had made claim on behalf of the land losers before the Land Acquisition Officer and had received the compensation amount on their behalf.

It is not the case of the first informant that he had received Laxman vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130489276/
2 any complaint from the land losers in this regard.

sentences.text:
The allegation made against the NC:
2024:KHC-K:4779 petitioner, who is a practicing advocate and a notary appointed by the Union of India, is not supported by any material.

5. Section 13 of the Notaries Act reads as follows:
"13. Cognizance of offence.-- (1) No court shall take cognizance of any offence committed by a notary in the exercise or purported exercise of his functions under this Act save upon complaint in writing made by an officer authorised by the Central Government or a State Government by general or special order in this behalf.
(2) No magistrate other than a presidency magistrate or a magistrate of the first class shall try an offence punishable under this Act."
6.

Though the criminal case has been registered in the year 2022, till date no sanction has been obtained by the competent authority as provided under Section 13 of the Notaries Act to prosecute the petitioner.

Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that continuation of NC:
2024:KHC-K:4779 impugned criminal proceedings as against the petitioner would amount to abuse of process of law.
Accordingly, the following order is passed:
ORDER The criminal petition is allowed.

The entire proceedings in Crime No.154/2022 registered by Muddebihal Police Station, Vijayapur for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 409, 465,
467, 468, 471 read with Section 149 of IPC, pending before the Court of Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Muddebihal as against the petitioner stands quashed.
